label: prf:positive-definite-dagger
title: Proof that the Frobenius dagger is positive-definite
html:
Write h(f, g) = \int_A \mu(S(f) \otimes g) and L_x for left multiplication by x \in A.

Adjoint of L_x. Since S is anti-multiplicative, S(x a) = S(a)\,S(x), so

  h(L_x a, b) = \int_A \mu\bigl(S(a)\,S(x) \otimes b\bigr)
  = \int_A \mu\bigl(S(a) \otimes S(x)\, b\bigr) = h(a, L_{S(x)} b).

Uniqueness. If U is R-linear with h(L_x a, b) = h(a, U b) for all a, b, put c = U b - S(x) b. Then h(c, c) = h(c, U b) - h(c, S(x) b) = h(L_x c, b) - h(L_x c, b) = 0, so c = 0 by positive definiteness.

Involution and contravariance. Applying the adjoint formula to S(x) gives h(L_{S(x)} a, b) = h(a, L_{S^2(x)} b) = h(a, L_x b), using S^2 = \mathrm{id}. Applying it to x y gives h(L_{xy} a, b) = h(a, L_{S(y)} L_{S(x)} b), using S(xy) = S(y)\,S(x). The involution S^2 = \mathrm{id} is a hypothesis: for a pivotal Hopf algebra S^2 is conjugation by the pivotal element, which is the identity only in the involutory case.

Scalars. For r \in R, S(r \cdot 1) = r\,S(1) = r \cdot 1, so on \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R the dagger is S and fixes every scalar.

Positivity. f^{\dagger} \circ f = \int_A \mu(S(f) \otimes f) = h(f, f), which is positive for f \neq 0 by hypothesis. \square

Positivity does not follow from non-degeneracy of the pairing: a non-degenerate form can have isotropic vectors. On R^2 the form \langle x, y\rangle = x_1 y_2 + x_2 y_1 is non-degenerate and \langle e_1, e_1\rangle = 0. The positivity of h is therefore an input, as in the GNS construction, where it is the positivity of the state ([kock2004], Ch. 2, for the Frobenius side); over \mathbb{C} and on non-involutive Hopf \ast-algebras where S^2 \neq \mathrm{id}_A, the same proof applies verbatim with S replaced by the conjugate-linear \ast-involution x \mapsto x^* in h_*(a, b) = \int_A a^* b, using (x^*)^* = x in place of S^2 = \mathrm{id}_A and r^* \cdot 1_A on scalars.
